facts.raw_span: asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove on the left side of his forehead, frontal scalp, and vertex area
Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning on the left scalp area
2 long, curved-line, depressed, alopecic patches on the left side of the vertex and frontal scalp area extending to the left eyebrow
lesions measured (length × width) 7 × 2 cm and 6 × 1 cm, respectively
Dermoscopic examination of the alopecic area revealed several short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation
broken hairs were not seen
result of a hair pull test was negative
Histopathologic examination shows predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis
inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis
Direct immunofluorescence: Positive with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels
Antinuclear antibody: Negative
Antidouble-stranded DNA antibody: Negative

concepts.why: The patient's presentation of asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin grooves, localized linear hair loss, and hair thinning, along with histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis, are consistent with discoid lupus erythematosus.

The patient's presentation of linear hair loss and hair thinning, along with dermoscopic findings of short vellus hairs, yellow dots, and honeycomb hyperpigmentation, are consistent with lichen planopilaris.
The patient's presentation of linear hair loss and hair thinning, along with the location and shape of the lesions, are consistent with frontal fibrosing alopecia.
The patient's presentation of asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin grooves, along with histopathologic findings of lymphocytic infiltrates and lobular panniculitis, are consistent with morphea.

rationales.F01: The presence of an asymptomatic, arc-shaped, depressed skin groove is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus and frontal fibrosing alopecia.
rationales.F02: Localized linear hair loss and hair thinning are common features of lichen planopilaris and frontal fibrosing alopecia.
rationales.F08: The histopathologic examination showing predominant lymphocytic infiltrates in perifollicular and periappendageal regions of the dermis and lobular panniculitis is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F09: The presence of inflammatory infiltrates between adipocytes with hyaline fat necrosis in the subcutis is more typical of morphea.
rationales.F10: The positive direct immunofluorescence with granular deposition of IgG, IgA, IgM, C3, C1q, and fibrinogen in the dermal blood vessels is more typical of discoid lupus erythematosus.
rationales.F11: The absence of antinuclear antibody makes discoid lupus erythematosus less likely.
rationales.F12: The absence of antidouble-stranded DNA antibody makes discoid lupus erythematosus less likely.
